text:
maria: heads-up — seeing weird partial-json + mojibake on Android client when streaming SSE from the hosted API. Small JSON objects (like {"id":...,"text":...}) are being split in the middle of a UTF-8 multibyte char, then we parse and get "�" chars. anyone run into this with OkHttp/EventSource?

alex: yup. common when you naively convert each chunk to String() without carrying over incomplete bytes. OkHttp gives you bytes; if a multibyte sequence is split you need to keep the trailing bytes and prepend them to the next chunk before decoding.

pranav: also check your decoder: Charset.forName("UTF-8").newDecoder() and use ByteBuffer + CharBuffer so you can call decode() with CoderResult.UNDERFLOW handling. If you just do new String(bytes) you lose state.

jess: for Kotlin coroutines/Flow clients we solved it by keeping a small ByteArrayBuffer and only emit when we have a full JSON object (fast-path: check for balanced braces). Pseudocode:
```kotlin
val carry = ByteArrayOutputStream()
source.forEach { chunk ->
  carry.write(chunk)
  val decoded = decoder.decode(ByteBuffer.wrap(carry.toByteArray()), charBuffer, false)
  val s = charBuffer.toString()
  // try to extract complete JSON objects from s, leave remainder in carry
}
```

maria: thanks — interesting. we are using kotlinx-coroutines + Channels with capacity 64. Could channel backlog be exacerbating the issue?

alex: backlog alone doesn't corrupt bytes, but if you convert each chunk independently later (after buffering) and you dropped the tail between buffers you'll see corruption. Also ensure you are not re-encoding strings across different charsets (e.g., logging with Windows-1252 somewhere).

pranav: another angle: OkHttp’s EventSource / sse libs sometimes give you text frames already decoded (String). If you use that API, you can't recover split multibyte sequences. Use the raw ResponseBody.source() stream and read bytes yourself.

maria: ah — we are using a third-party EventSource which gives onEvent(String). that explains it. we'll switch to a raw byte stream. any tips for backpressure so UI doesn't stutter?

jess: in Flow/Coroutines: handle IO on Dispatchers.IO and use buffer(Channel.BUFFERED) or conflate() depending on semantics. For streaming tokens you usually want to suspend producers when consumer can't keep up: use a Rendezvous channel or set small capacity and let producer suspend. Example:
```kotlin
val ch = Channel<ByteArray>(capacity = 1) // backpressure - producer will suspend
producer.launch { while (running) ch.send(nextChunk()) }
consumer.launch { for (b in ch) process(b) }
```

alex: also consider incremental JSON parsing instead of string assembly. Moshi JsonReader can parse from BufferedSource and handle partial input; you feed it bytes and advance when a complete object is seen. That avoids large intermediate strings.

maria: great — one more: retries. if connection drops mid-json and we reconnect, whats the recommended approach? drop partial carry and request the model to resend? or resume from last token?

pranav: depends on semantics. For deterministic streaming (e.g., logs) you can resume with Range-like token offsets. For model streaming it's best to treat each SSE session as ephemeral: on reconnect ask server for a fresh generation or include last-accepted-id to dedupe. Hosted API supports idempotency/continuation headers? check the API docs or attach a prompt-id.

jess: pragmatic: on reconnect drop partial buffer and show a small system token like "[reconnecting — content may be incomplete]". For production UI, try to show partial tokens but mark as provisional.

maria: thanks all. i'll prototype: switch to raw ResponseBody.source(), implement CharsetDecoder with ByteBuffer carry, use a Channel capacity=1 to force backpressure, and fall back to full restart on reconnects. i'll open a PR for review.

devex-bot: CI queued for branch maria/sse-android-fix — run tests: unit stream-parsing, end-to-end reconnect, large-utf8-blobs.

alex: ping me on the PR for a quick review. and add a tiny integration test that splits multibyte chars randomly across chunks. saved us before.

maria: will do. thanks!
